newsitem.title: USA: Flight attendants continue to slam ValuJet.
newsitem.headline: Flight attendants continue to slam ValuJet.

text.p: The Association of Flight Attendants continued its attacks on ValuJet Inc, saying the grounded airline misled the U.S Department of Transportation (DOT) regarding key manager's qualifications and recent personnel changes.
The union is seeking to oust ValuJet's Chairman Robert Priddy and President Lewis Jordan, alleging they are incompetent and unfit to run the airline.
The discount carrier suspended operations in June amid the intense regulatory scrutiny that arose after the fatal crash of ValuJet Flight 592 in the Florida Everglades in May.
ValuJet was not immediately available to comment on the union's allegations, but previously discounted the claims as a labor bargaining ploy.
The union, in a filing to the DOT on Tuesday, alleged that ValuJet's former vice president of maintenance, David Gentry, was not qualified for the position.

The flight attendants also alleged that ValuJet misled the DOT about Gentry's experience and only removed him from responsibility for maintenance oversight this month, after the union raised concerns with regulators.
Gentry, who oversaw ValuJet's maintenance operations at the time of the Flight 592 crash, has since been reassigned to vice president of special operations, the union said.
The union also said that ValuJet's recent filings with regulators indicate the airline has not filled two key management positions, including the director of vendor maintenance oversight.

"In light of the company's attempts to blame a maintenance vendor for the Everglades accident, it is unconscionable for Priddy and Jordan to seek to resume flight operations with the vendor oversight position unfilled," said Patricia Friend, AFA International President.
